dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: OK, Nam. You have five minutes. You can start now.
dialogue.reading: oʊˈkeɪ, ˈnɑːm. juː ˈhæv ˈfaɪv ˈmɪnɪts. juː kən ˈstɑːrt ˈnaʊ.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Good morning, everyone. First of all, I'd like to thank you for coming.
dialogue.reading: ɡʊd ˈmɔːrnɪŋ, ˈɛvriwʌn. ˈfɜːrst əv ˈɔːl, aɪd ˈlaɪk tə ˈθæŋk juː fər ˈkʌmɪŋ.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Next, I'll show the outline. My presentation has three sections.
dialogue.reading: ˈnɛkst, aɪl ˈʃoʊ ði ˈaʊtlaɪn. maɪ ˌprɛzənˈteɪʃən ˈhæz ˈθriː ˈsɛkʃənz.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Can you read the outline slide for me?
dialogue.reading: kən juː ˈriːd ði ˈaʊtlaɪn ˈslaɪd fər miː?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Sure. First, the introduction. Then, my survey. Finally, the results and what they mean.
dialogue.reading: ˈʃʊr. ˈfɜːrst, ði ˌɪntrəˈdʌkʃən. ˈðɛn, maɪ ˈsɜːrveɪ. ˈfaɪnəli, ðə rɪˈzʌlts ənd ˈwʌt ðeɪ ˈmiːn.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Nice and clear. How will you start the introduction?
dialogue.reading: ˈnaɪs ənd ˈklɪr. ˈhaʊ wɪl juː ˈstɑːrt ði ˌɪntrəˈdʌkʃən?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: I'll say, "Let's start with my research question: how do Thai students use English outside class?"
dialogue.reading: aɪl ˈseɪ, ˈlɛts ˈstɑːrt wɪð maɪ ˈriːsɜːrtʃ ˈkwɛstʃən: ˈhaʊ duː ˈtaɪ ˈstuːdənts ˈjuːz ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˌaʊtˈsaɪd ˈklæs?

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Good. And when you finish that section?
dialogue.reading: ˈɡʊd. ənd ˈwɛn juː ˈfɪnɪʃ ðæt ˈsɛkʃən?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: I'll say, "Let's move on to my survey," and go to the next slide.
dialogue.reading: aɪl ˈseɪ, ˈlɛts ˈmuːv ˈɑːn tə maɪ ˈsɜːrveɪ, ənd ˈɡoʊ tə ðə ˈnɛkst ˈslaɪd.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Perfect. Words like "Moving on to…" help the audience follow you.
dialogue.reading: ˈpɜːrfɪkt. ˈwɜːrdz laɪk ˈmuːvɪŋ ˈɑːn tuː… ˈhɛlp ði ˈɔːdiəns ˈfɑːloʊ juː.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Great. I'll use one at the start of every section.
dialogue.reading: ˈɡreɪt. aɪl ˈjuːz ˈwʌn ət ðə ˈstɑːrt əv ˈɛvri ˈsɛkʃən.
